summary: This morning's risk-off call (confidence 0.55) held up on day one. SPY closed at 715.87, about -1.96% from the 730.20 reference and 1.94% below the 730.02 200-day line, so the 'one more down close' I flagged has happened: the regime filter turns off at the next run, and VOO's and VTI's shared SPY stop is TRIPPED in close.json. The account fell 1.60% (equity 621.35 to 611.38) against SPY's -1.96% (spy_value 571.60 to 560.38). Since 11-10 the account is -1.79% against SPY's -4.54%. The favored Staples names only partly sheltered: WMT -0.97% on a beat-and-raise print, KR -1.61%, SAM -2.24%, all down with the market. This is one session of a five-session grade, so the call is not graded yet.
broken_theses: Staples as shelter is only partly confirmed. My favor list assumed Staples would hold up, and the held Staples names fell 1-2.2%, less than SPY but not flat. WMT slipped 0.97% even after raising guidance. close.json has no XLP or XLU closes, so I can't say whether the sectors themselves beat SPY. The 'favor' tilt was relative, and it should be described that way rather than as a hedge.

Breadth counterweight: in the morning note I gave RSP (21d -0.20%, 3.56% above its 200-day) as a reason to keep confidence at 0.55. close.json has no RSP close, so I can't tell whether breadth broke today. That item stays open rather than counting as confirmed or refuted.
update: For the next run the regime filter is off: SPY is at 715.87 against a 200-day of about 730 (the line will be re-computed, but it can't plausibly move 2% in one session), so only defensive ETFs can be bought, and VOO/VTI (about 23.3% of equity, both tripped) fall under the PM's pre-committed combined sale. The risk-off case still stands on what we know: SPY -1.96% today on top of 5d -3.90%, the 200-day line broken, and in the morning packet vol at 23.1% realized with VIXY 5d +20.5%. I should still keep tomorrow's confidence moderate and not raise it on today's move alone. SPY is now about 5.8% below where it was six sessions ago (from the morning 5d -3.90% plus today's drop), and after drops that size a 5-session bounce of more than 1% is a real risk to a risk-off grade. My last two graded risk-on calls (11-10, 11-11) were wrong by -2.3% and -3.9%, and my 52.9% hit rate does not beat 'always neutral' at 47.1% by much. So tomorrow I'll weigh VIXY's 5-day change and HYG/LQD against their 200-day lines more heavily than price momentum. A VIXY 5d turning negative or HYG recovering would move me to neutral. TLT rising while SPY falls would change the bonds view, which matters now that bonds are among the few buyable sleeves. No Reviewer lesson names the Market Analyst, so none shaped this review.
